mini_agent 2.0.1 fixes problems found when people new to mini_agent ran it from scratch, and
in real use after 2.0.0. There is nothing new to learn: commands, settings and files stay as
they are.

Fixed

- A stopped tool command can clean up. When you stop a task (Ctrl+C, a service stop, closing
  the terminal) or a command reaches its 120 s limit, the command on macOS and Linux now gets
  the signal first (SIGINT for Ctrl+C, SIGTERM at the time limit) and 2 s to finish, and only
  then is killed; a second stop during those 2 s kills it at once. In 2.0.0 it was killed at
  once, so it could not delete temporary files or write a last line. On Windows the command
  is ended at once, as before, with what it started; when taskkill cannot run or fails, the
  command itself is still ended, but programs it started may keep running (end them in Task
  Manager).
- Shorter tool calls on the screen. In the interactive modes, a call that writes a file shows
  its path and size instead of the whole file, and a long command or piece of code shows its
  first line and its size. A reply in the model's own tool-call markup is shown as a note in
  square brackets instead of raw markup. The session log, the approval prompt and what the
  model sees are unchanged.
- After `mini_agent setup` with offline mode, the suggested first task is one that offline
  mode can answer: `mini_agent "Compute 3**7."`, on a line of its own so that it can be
  pasted as it is.
- The model is told which command starts Python on your computer (python3, python, or on
  Windows the py launcher; with none of them on PATH, the path of the Python that runs
  mini_agent, quoted for the shell), so it can use that one instead of a `python` that is
  missing or the Windows placeholder that only opens the Microsoft Store.
- Offline mode says so, once per task in each run, when it replays the closest recorded step
  instead of an exact match, for example after you changed a prompt, a skill or an approval
  rule: such a change has no effect offline.
- The calculator refuses any integer value of more than about 300,000 digits, numbers written
  in the expression and intermediate results included, and an expression whose integer
  values together pass about 2.4 million digits. Where it can, it refuses before computing:
  `(10**10000)**10000` is now refused at once; in 2.0.0 it ran for more than 30 s, and one
  more level of power would fill memory.

Worth knowing

- A run started from a script as a background job (`mini_agent "..." &` in `sh`), without
  `--keep-alive`, ignores Ctrl+C because the shell tells background jobs to; stop it with
  `kill -TERM <pid>`. The README says this now.
